- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate early in horizon; reduce forecast peaks, especially in first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model underestimates, especially in late horizon; increase forecast tail (last 5–7 days) to capture downside risk.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment = 1.00 followed by 0.00), leading to over-forecasting in next 3–5 days; apply dampening factor to post-spike periods.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >2σ above history mean, reduce by 15–30% in next 7 days unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to over-optimism in early days (days 1–10) when sentiment is bullish; cap early forecast growth at 1.2x recent average.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00/1.00 alternation, model tends to misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth transitions.
